newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels fire shots at police.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels fire shots at police.

text.p: Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages for the 41st day fired several shots on Monday at armoured police vehicles going by the besieged Japanese ambassador's home, police said.
Police said several bullets hit one of the three armoured vehicles passing the residence.
"One bullet ricocheted off the front window and the others hit the back (part of the vehicle)," one policeman at the site said.

It was the first time in the 41-day siege that there had been danger of anybody being hit by gunfire. On previous occasions, the rebels fired warning shots into the air hours after police manoeuvres around the building.

The gunshots -- heard at about 4:45 p.m. local time (2145 GMT) -- put about 200 security forces on alert and sent several police diving for cover behind the residence's walls and inside their armoured vehicles.
Police trained their sights on the residence but did not reply with shots.
Within minutes of the shots, most police and all the armoured vehicles withdrew from the area around the residence.

The shooting happened during a procession of armoured personnel carriers and scores of special forces training semi-automatic weapons on the residence. They circled the diplomatic site several times as a helicopter hovered overhead.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels shouted at the police aboard the armoured cars, and security forces in one vehicle responded with obscene gestures, witnesses said.
The rebels then fired several rounds from the ambassador's home, which they have held since they stormed it during a party on Dec. 17.
The police and their armoured vehicles returned to the site about 5:15 p.m. local time (2215 GMT) and made another parade around the fortified compound. There were no shots fired that time.
